Project Flamingo - Spreading feathers of hope.

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Women trying to cope with breast cancer diagnoses often face agonising long waiting times for surgery , but a group of surgeons decided that something had to be done giving timely surgery.

Unique Selling Point:
When faced with the heartbreaking, stretched out and often chaotic journey of a breast cancer patient in the public sector many women find it daunting and feel isolated in their struggle with the diagnoses. Dr Liana Roodt, surgeon at the Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town decided that something needed to be done. Many of these women were subjected to agonizingly long waiting times for surgery. The simple yet profoundle effective idea of "Catch up Surgeries" and "Pamper packs" was born.

Summary:
Timely surgery for newly diagnosed beast cancer patients= currently achieved by funded catch-up surgery lits, performed at Groote Schuur and Tygerberg hospital (paying for theatre time and nursing staff) The project started with surgeons doing the surgery pro-bono and initially funding it from their own pockets. This was to compensate for the tremendous strain on theatre and staff resources that have led t a waiting time up to 12 weeks for surgery. The Project Flamingo was initiated when the Amabele Belles Dragonboat Racing team pledged the first donation. It was Kismet. Project Flamingo has subsequently changed hundreds of lives.
The project has been expanded to to patients urgently requiring surgery at GSH for colorectal as well.

SCRIPT : Project Flamingo



PROMO 1 11


The healthcare sector is taking strain and breast cancer patients can wait months for life-saving surgery. But a dedicated team of doctors is hope to some desperate women.
PROMO 2 11”
A breast cancer diagnosis is a woman’s worst nightmare, and long waiting lists mean many don’t get the surgery they desperately need. But one young surgeon’s initiative is bringing hope to many patients.
PROMO 3 11”


A ground-breaking initiative at Groote Schuur hospital in Cape Town sees selfless doctors and nursing staff bringing relief to an overburdened healthcare system.


Up Sound : Patricia Hector



Claire V/O




Patricia Hector
Cancer Survivor


Claire V/O






Up Sound Patricia



Claire Link


















I woke up one the morning and I did that, oh whats’ this,

On that ordinary morning in 2016 Patricia Hector made a frightening discovery: a lump in her breast.


I kind of made myself happy for want of a better word that its probably just fatty tissue however my mom had breast cancer.

Fearing the worst, Patricia visited the breast clinic at Groote Schuur Hospital, where biopsies confirmed her nightmare was true: she had aggressive breast cancer that needed surgery.

I just dropped my head oh my goodness it really is what it is.

Hundreds of women get diagnosed with breast cancer every year at Groote Schuur hospital in Cape Town. With limited resources and time running out for many of these women, an innovative idea from a young surgeon has brought relief to an overwhelmed health care system.
Claire V/O







In 2010, a young doctor fresh out of community service joined the surgical team at Groote Schuur. Dr Liana Roodt immediately saw the desperate need to reduce the time that women, like Patricia, were waiting to receive life-saving breast surgery. From her insight sprang Project Flamingo.


Liana Roodt
Dr Liana Roodt
Surgeon: Groote Schuur Hospital


04:42 Let me tell you that when you don’t know what you’re getting yourself into and you just jumped in first, then you make it work
Claire V/O












Liana Roodt










Overburdened theatres are unable to keep up with the demands of the weekly surgical lists. So Roodt and her colleagues began to perform ‘catch-up’ surgeries on weekends and public holidays to reduce the overflow.

06:58 In the beginning, it was quite a struggle. Are we going to have enough money to pay the nursing staff to come and help us in theatre or are we going to have enough surgeons? Are we going to have enough anaesthetists. Anaesthetists were often covered by friends that owed me a favour, once they've done the list once they enjoyed it so much that they kept on coming for more.
Claire V/O










The team worked pro bono and initially funded the project from their own pockets. They shared patients’ stories by word of mouth and slowly Project Flamingo took flight. Today, it involves 40 surgeons and anaesthetists.

UPSOUND: Lydia Cairncross





Claire V/O






Claire V/O



Lydia Cairncross

00:26 We see about 600 patients with new breast cancer diagnoses every year. And those patients need surgery.

Dr Lydia Cairncross has been the head of oncology and endocrinology at Groote Schuur since 2014. She has been part of the Project Flamingo core team from its inception.

06:22 If we didn’t have Project Flamingo, we would have a 22 to 24 week wait for breast cancer surgery.
Claire V/O






Dr Liana Roodt

Not only can a long wait for surgery be fatal, but it can also be emotionally devastating for patients.

You can see what the impact was on the patient’s psyche, the patients emotional wellbeing, and not only the patient, but the ripple effect it has on the whole family and whole family, structure of the patient. `Their tremendous fear, the tremendous anxiety the feeling of helplessness.
Lydia Cairncross.
Dr Lydia Cairncross
Head: Oncology and Endocrinology: GSH

Project Flamingo is a very important project because it assists us to improve the waiting time for surgery . 12:28 So while yes, we are giving up our time and it was hard to leave my children, at least today we have done something practical and real for women.

04:42 It is fantastic to know that we are using our time and our energy to make an immediate difference. There is a sense of sadness as well though, because we know in many parts of the country, this is not possible.
Claire V/O



Patricia Hector







Project Flamingo allowed Patricia to have the urgent surgery that she needed.



We were about 8 of us and we referred to as the Flamingo ladies.





Claire V/O

On the Flamingo list the week of our visit is fifty-one year old Faldielah Balaskas.. We meet her on a sunny Friday morning at her home in Athlone Cape Town as she is preparing to be admitted for her surgery.
Faldielah Balaskas

10:15 Today is a big day , today I’m being booked in, I must be…. . The operation is taking place tomorrow.
Faldielah Balaskas
Cancer Patient


I am feeling anxious, I’m feeling nervous and I’m feeling excited because I needed the operation done so I can start with my healing process and go on with my life.
Claire V/O

One of the surgeons spreading feathers of hope is Dr Francois Malherbe. He will form part of Faldielah’s surgical team.
Dr Francois Malherbe
Surgeon: Groote Schuur Hospital


04:14 I found a lump in her breast on the right hand side.
01:57 So because she had a more aggressive cancer, we gave her chemo therapy first, she is not going to wait long for her surgery.
Claire V/O


Faldielah is grappling with cancer alone. Having no children, and her husband of 25 years suddenly passed away earlier this year.
Faldielah Balaskas




11:16 I’ve lost the love of my life. It's the 12th of July. 15:21 10:15 It’s been a tough year.
11:16. Me not working, my losing my husband. was a tough journey. But, I am a survivor and I’m a fighter , I have always been since the age of 13. I’ve been looking out for myself.
Claire V/O
With her bag packed and having greeted her family, Faldielah begins her journey.

Dr Malherbe

We are going to do a full mastectomy for her. We are going to remove the breast with what is left of the tumour after the chemo.
Claire Link



Claire V/O


Claire Question
It is Saturday morning here at Groote Schuur hospital and Faldielah is here to receive her life saving surgery.


After two hours the surgery is complete.

How did the surgery go? Are you confident that it went well?
Yes, we are feeling confident. I think it went really well.Since Faldielah already had chemo therapy after the surgery probably the only thing that is left for her to do is heal and recover and this would be the end of her treatment. journey.
Claire V/O









A mastectomy is life-saving surgery, but it can severely impact a woman’s sense of femininity. Under the leadership of Project Flamingo Director Michelle Rennie, a small group of volunteers provides pamper packs to give comfort and help restore self-esteem.
Michelle Rennie.

Director: Project Flamingo

We hand the pamper packs out to all the women diagnosed with cancers, but what I have seen are women who end up in that passage waiting for their appointment cards, they will see someone or sit next to someone who has also got a pack, giving one another a hug, exchanging phone numbers and I realized that the pamper pack is actually gone further than just this handover. It’s actually been connected a whole lot of people and something like that restores your dignity as a woman.
Claire V/O


But perhaps the biggest gift that Project Flamingo has given to women like Patricia Hector is time to spend with her children and grandchildren.
Patricia Hector


We can never, ever, ever , words or deeds or money if you ever had it could not repay for what they have sacrificed. I’m getting emotioal.
Liana Roodt
Being in the privileged position of witnessing someone else’s journey and for them to trust you with that journey is a ja, really a tremendous privilege. Not only do I believe more in the the goodness of of life , but I believe more in people’s, in people’s capacity to do good.
